evidence: Read cold in CONTEXT.txt: the draft is the last sentence of the "Temporary Separation." paragraph and appears once, verbatim: "You want to be able to let the quiet little preferences that you have bubble up to the surface and know for sure that you’re not going by what your social group would want you to do." It comes after "As you differentiate, you learn to tell which of those apply." CHANGE: it is Emulate's sentence for the paragraph's last one, and the quote marks around social are gone (checked: none around social in the draft or in its place in CONTEXT.txt). FLOW: it reads as the aim of the separation; "be able to" picks up "learn to tell", and the same step from "which of those apply" to the aim was already in the sentence it replaces, so the change does not make the jump worse. PRONOUNS: "that you have" points at the preferences, "you" is the reader throughout, and "your social group" is the "people or group that you normally would get answers from" of the first sentence (C02 clear). MEANING vs SOURCE.txt: kept are the quieter preferences surfacing ("quiet little preferences that you have bubble up to the surface") and being sure they are the reader's own and not the group's ("know for sure that you’re not going by what your social group would want you to do"). Judged shifts, each small: "just echoing your social group" (his "social echo") becomes going by what the group would want you to do, which narrows echo to following the group's wishes but is the same check in this section (people who don't know what they want until they hear what someone else wants); "so you can be sure" becomes "and know for sure", so the surfacing and the certainty are two coordinate aims instead of one enabling the other; "quieter" becomes "quiet little". None adds a fact or a claim about anyone (C03, C04 absent). TELLS: I went through T01-T29 and C01-C04 and find none PRESENT. Nearest calls: T22 ("You want to be able to" anticipates what the reader wants) is not present because the sentence gives the reason for the separation, so it is not reassurance or instruction alone; T15 is not present because the changes are plain-speech and clause-level ("going by what ... would want you to do" for "echoing"), not rarer words swapped in for their own sake; T03 is not present because the jump from the previous sentence is the one the replaced sentence already made, set up by the heading label and "losing yourself"; T21 is not present because the two coordinated infinitives are one aim; T26 is not present because "want" twice in a sentence sets your wants against the group's, which is the section's theme; T29/T20/T28 are not present because it adds the aim (a new consideration, not a restatement) and ends on a plain long clause with no closer or uplift; T16 is not present because "not going by" is a plain negation with no "not X, it's Y"; T06 and T07 are not present because "bubble up to the surface" is the image the replaced sentence already had and "quiet little" is an adjective phrase from "quieter", not filler. Cosmetic only: "that you have bubble up" puts "have" and "bubble" side by side, a small snag, and the sentence is longer (37 words against 24). LINTER: two findings, both accepted. "D9 follows the source order": one sentence with two points in the only order the sense allows (the preferences surface, then you can be sure they are yours), each part specific to this section, so T13 and T09 are clear. "E36/E41 heavy second person": the whole section speaks to "you" (the list items and the neighbouring sentences), the draft has 5 you-forms in 37 words (13.5 per 100), less dense than the 5 in 24 words (about 21 per 100) of the sentence it replaces, and the sentence states the aim of a step rather than a run of coaching lines. Note on the writer's ledger: its T14 and T15 evidence says this sentence puts back the author's point or words, but the_change records no such fix here (the sentence is Emulate's as is, bar the quote marks), so I judged T14 and T15 on the draft itself.
